newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Profit-taking ends Hungary bourse record bull-run.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking ends Hungary bourse record bull-run.

text.p: Hungarian shares on Friday reversed a 14-day record bull run, which raised the BUX index some 25 percent, as the buying side weakened and several investors closed positions, traders said.
The Budapest Stock Exchange's (BSE) BUX index closed at 4,714.50 points, down 10.09.
"This was not a real correction yet," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings. "But the 'madness', which lasted for many days, seems to stop, and that's completely normal."
"Very many speculants did at the beginning of the session, what they usually did recently, and purchased, but buying interest altogether was lower (then recently)," he added.

Oil and gas company MOL, one of the main beneficiaries of the BSE's recent rally was one of the still numerous shares to extend gains, rising to 2,700 forints during the session and closing at 2,600 forints, up 175.
"MOL is one paper which even domestic investors trust," said Marton Olah of Creditanstalt, adding that Hungarian investors sold several stocks to lock in profits.
Other traders said foreign investors also closed positions, pushing down some of the shares.
Traders said that the drug maker Richter was one of the major losers of the day, finishing at 10,225 forints, down 745, on correction.
Traders added that Friday's drops may be signall a wave of larger corrections, but the direction of the prices depended on world and regional stock market trends and the performance of the dollar.

BUX index futures dropped for almost all maturities, by 40 to 93 points. The December 1997 maturity closed 42.50 points lower, at 5,550, while December 1998 BUX futures ended up by 15 points, at 6,125.
